nigeria.title: ‘Teachers, doctors won’t pay tax when I become gov’
nigeria.description: By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo LAGOS—Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr. Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes, if elected governor, saying his administration will use increased Federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and welfare of residents. Doherty, who made the promise during an interview on a Channels Television programme, said he would also introduce a tax card that would enable residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation. He said: “When I am governor, I will transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two groups will not pay tax. “Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation. This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you.” The PDP candidate also promised free education, saying the funds available to the state would enable him to implement the policy. Justifying the proposed tax exemption for doctors, he said: “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break.” He described teachers as critical to the state’s future, arguing that they must receive proper training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities. Doherty further condemned attacks on political activities and disclosed that some people he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge. He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he would visit the Department of State Services, DSS. nigeria.description: …₦382.9m disbursed to 31 businesses By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has secured approval for ₦1.041 billion in intervention funding for small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs), in a move aimed at expanding businesses, stimulating job creation and improving access to affordable credit. Of the amount, ₦382.9 million has already been disbursed to 29 micro-enterprises and two small and medium-scale businesses, while another ₦206.7 million in approved applications is undergoing documentation ahead of disbursement. The state government also announced a review of the remuneration of ad-hoc workers engaged by the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA), with the new payment structure taking effect from November 2026. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, who disclosed the developments during the weekly briefing on the State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia, said the SME intervention was being implemented through the Bank of Industry (BOI). Kanu, represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Fredinald Ekeoma, said the initiative was part of Governor Alex Otti’s administration’s efforts to strengthen the state’s productive sector and create sustainable employment opportunities. Providing further details, Commissioner for Industries and SMEs, Mazi Mike Akpara, said the outstanding approved facilities would be released once beneficiaries fulfilled the necessary conditions, including documentation and provision of guarantors and collateral, where applicable. He stressed that access to the intervention was not restricted by political affiliation, insisting that any genuine business operating in Abia was eligible. “Whether you belong to the Labour Party, PDP or APC, we are not concerned about that. Once you are doing business in Abia and can provide evidence of your business operations, you are eligible to benefit. “SMEs are the engine of the economy, and this initiative is intended to encourage and strengthen them,” Akpara said. He said interested businesses could access the programme through the Ministry of Industries and SMEs at the Nnamdi Azikiwe Secretariat, Umuahia, or the BOI office in Aba. Akpara described the facility as a major relief for local entrepreneurs, given its relatively low interest rates of 8.5 per cent for overdrafts and 7.5 per cent for other facilities, with a three-year repayment period. He contrasted the rates with commercial bank lending rates, which he said could rise to between 28 and 30 per cent, arguing that the intervention would ease the financing burden on businesses and improve their capacity to expand. In another development, Kanu said the Ministry of Industries and SMEs had verified and documented more than 110 workshops and 120 shops at the Ohiya-Umuogo-Nsukwe Industrial Cluster. nigeria.title: Wike to opposition: Stop creating chaos to blame Tinubu
nigeria.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, yesterday, accused opposition political parties of deliberately fomenting trouble to make it appear that President Bola Tinubu is responsible for political violence ahead of the 2027 elections. Wike made the allegation during the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) in the FCT at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja. The minister, who expressed confidence in the APC’s chances in the upcoming elections, claimed that opposition parties knew they had already lost and were creating political tension to discredit the ruling party. Wike said: “You have what it takes to win this election. The other parties know. Let me just tell you the simple truth. The other parties know they have lost the election. “What are they doing now? What they are doing now is to foment crisis—foment problems to make it look as if it is the government; it is the presidential candidate of the APC party who is fomenting trouble. “They (opposition) are the ones causing trouble. You (APC PCC) don’t need to cause trouble because you have already won the election. “They (opposition parties) foment trouble and report as if they are not the ones that have created that problem. So, we must be on alert.” Wike also told members of the Rainbow Coalition to make sure the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, do not get 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT in the January 16, 2027 general elections. He warned the members against assuming the contest was already won, saying the election was a chance for the APC to show its political strength in the territory. On how to sell the president’s record, he said: “You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign.” Wike also dared opposition politicians to set projects built before 2023 beside those delivered since Tinubu took office, arguing that the work going on in the city centre and the satellite towns spoke for itself. The senator, who is the APC senatorial candidate for the January 16, 2027 election, said there was a growing disconnect and misunderstanding between ordinary people in the North and the political elite. He urged the APC leadership and Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) to prioritise effective communication of President Bola Tinubu’s policies and ongoing reforms to Nigerians at the grassroots. The lawmaker also called on the party to identify and empower credible individuals and stakeholders with genuine grassroots influence in their respective constituencies rather than relying on what he described as “Abuja politicians” and entitled individuals disconnected from the people. In the statement titled, “A Clarion Call for Self-Reflection, Humility, and Grassroots Reconnection”, Suleiman said the party’s message was still not reaching ordinary Nigerians. nigeria.title: Don’t turn churches into campaign arena, Soludo cautions politicians
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State, on Sunday, cautioned politicians against turning churches and other places of worship into a political arena, stating that sacred spaces must remain neutral grounds for people of all political persuasions. Soludo made the remark during the 30th anniversary celebration of the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. Addressing the congregation, the governor stressed the need for the men of God to clearly separate politics from worship. According to Soludo, the place of worship should be a holy place where people of all political persuasion should come and worship God in peace. “It should not be a place for politics. There is a venue for politics. If you want to worship God, you have to go to the house of God. We must separate the two things clearly,” Soludo said. He recalled that six months before his election, he took a deliberate decision never to go to any church to cup a microphone to ask them to vote for him or to campaign. “It was a deliberate decision. I worshipped in the government house chapel until the election day and afterwards,” the governor stated. “We must never politicise the church. We must never politicise the place of worship. Politicians, keep off churches. Keep off places of worship. That’s a deliberate message, and it is my kind of consistency of character”, he further said. nigeria.title: Obi, Kwankwaso have God’s grace to dislodge Tinubu — Babachir Lawal
nigeria.description: A chieftain of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Babachir Lawal, has said Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Kwankwaso, his running mate, have God’s backing to defeat President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Lawal, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, who made the declaration during an appearance on Arise Television late Sunday, cited the “widespread support” Obi and Kwankwaso enjoyed as a pointer to God’s grace upon their lives. He said: “I have told everybody that talks to me that both Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have the grace of God upon their lives, which makes people like them. “The population likes them. They just show up in the market. They don’t hire people to come to their rallies. People just turn out at their own expense.” He said his experience in politics had enabled him to recognise signs that could favour the opposition alliance, adding that he previously occupied a similar position during the Muhammadu Buhari administration. “It’s not the first time I am in the position I am in now in politics. I have been in this position during Buhari’s time. Even this your president, I drove his system up to the primaries. “So I am a very skilled and experienced person in the game. I can see the signs and we know the loopholes. And we are working on the loopholes,’’ he said. Lawal expressed confidence that the NDC would defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. , saying the party had established structures and systems to achieve its objective. “We have an inside chance of toppling this government. We are inside and we know we will beat this government. “We know they are gone. We have put up structures and systems. I am 100 per cent confident,’’ he said. Lawal added that the responsibility of the party’s technical team was to convert the popularity of its presidential candidates into electoral success by ensuring that votes were protected and counted. “This grace that God has bestowed upon them, it’s our duty, the technical people, to harmonise and crystallise this thing into delivering it at the polling station and protecting the votes and ensuring it’s counted,” he said. Lawal dismissed concerns over recent departure of Yunusa Tanko, former national coordinator of the Obidient Movement; Nana Kazaure, Doyin Okupe, and the former NDC’s deputy national publicity secretary, from Obi’s camp, saying politicians were free to leave parties when their expectations were not met. I can remember Kashim Imam; he has also left. I remember Rauf Aregbesola, who was also with Bola Tinubu. But he has left. These are big politicians. Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state. The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion. Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December. On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas. The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited. The seventh project, covering 1.5 kilometres of the Kunuwal Road Network, was awarded to Swas Grade Limited. nigeria.title: Mimiko congratulates Aiyedatiwa on Silverbird award
nigeria.description: …Urges Ondo governor to deepen dividends of democracy By Dayo Johnson, Akure Former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has congratulated Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa on emerging as the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year. Mimiko described the award as recognition of the achievements recorded so far by the Aiyedatiwa administration and its efforts towards developing the state. The award was presented at the 20th edition of the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards held at Eko Hotels, Lagos. In a congratulatory message, the former governor urged Aiyedatiwa to see the recognition as a call to do more for the people of Ondo State and deepen the dividends of democracy. He said the honour by the Silverbird Group showed that the governor’s efforts were receiving recognition beyond the state. “This honour from the Silverbird Group is an acknowledgement that your efforts are being noticed and should, therefore, spur you to do more for the benefit of the greater majority of our compatriots in our dear state,” Mimiko said. He described Ondo State’s selection for the award among the 36 states as encouraging, noting that it reflected efforts being made across different sectors and communities. “It is encouraging to see Ondo State singled out among the 36 states for this award. It speaks to some work being done across sectors and locations in the state,” he added. Mimiko prayed for greater strength and wisdom for Aiyedatiwa as he continues to steer the affairs of the state. nigeria.title: Anambra Patriots endorse APGA-APC alliance, adopt Tinubu for 2027
nigeria.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A political pressure group in Anambra State, Anambra Patriots, APS, has endorsed the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, and the All Progressives Congress, APC, adopting President Bola Tinubu as its preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election. The group also declared its support for the re-election of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, and urged Ndigbo to support his political direction, including his backing for Tinubu. The convener of APS and Anambra State Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, disclosed the group’s position on Sunday during the Anambra Patriots Women Summit held in Awka, the state capital. Ezeobi expressed dissatisfaction with those criticising Soludo for aligning politically with Tinubu rather than supporting former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi. He argued that politics should be driven by interests rather than sentiments, insisting that Soludo’s decision to support Tinubu was in the interest of Ndigbo. “My problem with Ndigbo is that they don’t know how to play politics. We do politics of emotion instead of interest. In politics, you get what you contributed, not what you deserve. Politics is about interest,” he said. According to him, Soludo’s support for Tinubu was not motivated by personal gains but by what he described as the need for greater political inclusion of the South-East in national affairs. He said: “Prof. Soludo’s support for Tinubu is not for personal gain, but for the interest of Ndigbo. It is time for Ndigbo to come back to Nigeria. And Soludo is a professor; he has analysed Nigerian politics.” Ezeobi also argued that Soludo should not be criticised for his political choice, saying other ethnic groups had members supporting Obi without attracting similar criticism. He urged Anambra residents to recognise Soludo’s position as governor and support his political decisions, adding that backing Obi was not compulsory for every Igbo politician. “Why is everybody seeing Soludo as an enemy because he is supporting Tinubu? If we accept Soludo as our leader and governor in Anambra State, we must follow him anywhere he is pitching his political tent. It is not compulsory that we must support Peter Obi. Politics is not about sentiments,” he said. The commissioner also made several claims about the political relationship between Obi and Soludo, alleging that Obi had opposed Soludo’s governorship ambition on previous occasions. He cited the 2013, 2021 and 2025 governorship election cycles in Anambra, claiming that Obi had supported different political moves against Soludo, which ultimately failed. Ezeobi, however, maintained that Soludo had not insulted Obi but had only responded to comments he considered critical of Anambra State and APGA. nigeria.title: True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni
nigeria.description: … Backs YASA Foundation’s drive for inclusive society By Ogochukwu Agha lagos—The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has urged Nigerians, corporate organisations and philanthropists to support initiatives that empower vulnerable people, saying true fulfilment lies in making positive impact on others. The monarch spoke at the unveiling of the Yeye Afolashade Shona-Aluko (YASA) Foundation in Lagos, where he donated N5 million. Describing the foundation’s humanitarian mission as worthy of support, Oba Ogunwusi said: “What gives the greatest happiness in this world is a life of impact and fulfilment. Everybody is chasing money. But when you attain a certain level of wealth, you discover that money does not necessarily bring happiness. “The essence of life is what you can give to others.” Senator Sylvia Mthethwa of Eswatini urged governments and institutions to promote inclusive development, asking: “Are we developing societies in which everybody has an opportunity to participate or contribute and prosper?” She called for improved access to education, healthcare and employment for persons with disabilities. The Ooni’s wife, Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi, commended the foundation’s founder, urging her to remain committed to humanitarian service despite challenges. Earlier, Shona-Aluko said her youngest son’s disability inspired her intervention. She recalled employing eight specialised teachers to support him and other children at Ikeja High School for about nine years. She said the experience exposed the difficulties faced by families unable to afford specialised education. “YASA Foundation was born from a burden… a burden to give voice to the voiceless, strength to the weak, and to say boldly: ‘You are not forgotten,’” she said. The foundation focuses on inclusive education, healthcare, rehabilitation, assistive devices, vocational training and livelihood support. The event featured beneficiaries’ testimonies and recognition of Shona-Aluko by two international institutions. nigeria.title: Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated. Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks. Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations. Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system. She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival. “The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care. “However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said. She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified. Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays. “The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. As a result, valuable time is wasted accessing the wrong care when the patient could have been connected to the right facility through a coordinated system,” she added. nigeria.title: Drug insecurity threatens national security, pharmacists warn FG
nigeria.description: … Seeks 1% of seized drug trafficking assets to fund enforcement … Demands government control of medicine supply chain By Chioma Obinna The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a serious threat to Nigeria’s national security, urging the Federal Government to strengthen regulatory control of medicines and prevent the transfer of critical drug management responsibilities from public authorities to private interests. The society also called for the establishment of a special fund to tackle illicit financial flows in the healthcare sector, proposing that one per cent of assets seized from drug trafficking be dedicated to strengthening the enforcement activities of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged IJELE 2026, held from November 2 to 7 at the International Convention Centre, Awka, Anambra State. The conference, which brought together pharmacists and other stakeholders in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors, was held under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.” In the communiqué signed by the President, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba, and National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehin, the pharmacists maintained that medicines were not merely commercial commodities but matters of permanent regulatory control and national security. Citing Part I, Item 21 of the Second Schedule of the 1999 Constitution, the conference argued that the government’s responsibility for drug regulation and control could not be compromised by private-sector participation in the pharmaceutical supply chain. It cautioned against what it described as a private takeover of drug distribution responsibilities at the public-sector level, warning that such an arrangement could weaken inter-agency collaboration among the PCN, NAFDAC and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA). The communiqué stated: “Conference reminded Government that drugs are a matter of permanent regulatory control and National Security, which is why it is listed as Part I item 21, in the 2nd Schedule of the 1999 Constitution.” It added that while government could engage private-sector expertise in financing and technology deployment, it should not surrender its regulatory standing or the cooperation currently extended by relevant agencies to Federal Central Medical Stores and Federal Health Institutions. The PSN further called for the integration of community pharmacies into Nigeria’s national security architecture and the Nigeria Health Insurance Authority’s proposed Pharmacy First initiative. nigeria.title: 2027: Focus on issues, stop dancing at rallies, Pawpaw tells politicians
nigeria.description: Nollywood actor Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has urged Nigerian politicians to stop turning campaign rallies into entertainment shows, insisting that Nigerians need competent leaders who can deliver good governance. Iheme made the call in a post on his Instagram page on Monday, where he criticised the practice of politicians dancing on stage during campaign rallies. He urged political office seekers to use campaign platforms to showcase their achievements, demonstrate their capacity to lead and explain their plans to Nigerians, rather than engaging in choreography to entertain supporters. The actor said Nigerians needed competence, good governance and purposeful leadership, not political hype and entertainment. “We don’t need choreography. We need competence. We don’t need hype men. We need good governance. We don’t need entertainers. We need leaders,” he wrote. He challenged politicians to tell Nigerians what they had achieved and what they intended to do if elected. “Show us what you have done. Tell Nigerians what you will do. You are not going for Grammy,” he said. Iheme also warned politicians against dancing on campaign stages, declaring: “I don’t want to see you guys’ dance on stage again. business.title: Bitcoin Price Holds Near $65,000 as Nvidia Turmoil Drags Nasdaq Down 2.5%
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $65,000 as Nvidia Turmoil Drags Nasdaq Down 2.5% Bitcoin price traded near $65,000 on Monday afternoon, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, up more than 1% from where it sat at the time of this morning’s report. The world’s largest cryptocurrency held its ground even as a fresh round of selling in Nvidia dragged the Nasdaq down about 2.5%. The session was choppy. Bitcoin started the day near $64,000 after a weekend plunge to $62,000, then jumped to about $65,600 shortly after the U.S. stock market opened. The bounce faded within the hour, and the bitcoin price slipped back toward $64,000 as tech stocks extended their losses. Buyers stepped in there, and bitcoin has spent most of the afternoon trading around $65,000. Nvidia drags tech stocks lower while the bitcoin price steadies Nvidia was again the heaviest weight on markets. CNBC reported shortly after noon that the chipmaker’s board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO after he resigned last week. The board is instead focused on an investigation into whether Huang’s conduct compromised national security or company secrets, the report said. Earlier Monday, President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang return. Nvidia shares fell to a fresh intraday low after the report and closed down about 4%, a day before the company reports quarterly results. U.S. chipmakers dropped more than 5%. The Nasdaq Composite slid about 2.5% and the S&P 500 lost nearly 2%, with investors also bracing for Anthropic’s IPO later this week. Bitcoin did not follow stocks to their lows this time. As the Nasdaq sank to its worst levels of the day after the CNBC report, bitcoin stopped going down and held near $64,800. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Senate Agriculture Committee to Hear Trump’s CFTC Nominees Tuesday The Senate Agriculture Committee will hear President Donald Trump’s two nominees to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on Tuesday, a confirmation hearing that comes as the derivatives regulator has only one sitting commissioner. The committee scheduled the session for 3 p.m. Eastern in Room 106 of the Dirksen Senate Office Building. The White House sent the nominations to the Senate on Nov. 12. The nominees are Nathan Anonick of Virginia and Matthew Rowland of the District of Columbia. The hearing notice says to check back for live video, and the committee has not posted written testimony. Trump nominated the pair last week as part of a bipartisan slate for the CFTC and the Securities and Exchange Commission, a step that would begin to refill two regulators that have been operating short-handed. Who the nominees are Anonick serves on the Republican staff of the Senate Agriculture Committee under Chairman John Boozman of Arkansas. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. A 2023 committee release said Anonick joined the panel in 2022 to manage a portfolio that includes cryptocurrencies, futures markets and derivatives, and that he had previously worked at the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation as a resolution policy specialist. entertainment.title: Tems Is Officially a 12-Time Grammy Nominee!
entertainment.description: Tems is officially a 12-time Grammy nominee after securing four nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. Photo Credit: Tems/Instagram One, two, three… and now 12! Tems has added four more Grammy nominations to her record, bringing her career total to 12 ahead of the 69th Grammy Awards. The latest recognition also makes her the first Nigerian female artist to receive four nominations in a single Grammy year, with this year’s shortlist recognising her work across four categories. The Nigerian singer is in contention for Best Global Music Album with her 10-track EP, Love Is a Kingdom , and Best African Music Performance for “ Big Daddy ”. She has also earned nominations for Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “ What You Need ”. The four nominations give her one of the most extensive Nigerian representations at this year’s ceremony and bring her Grammy wins to two, following previous victories in 2023 and 2025. Her relationship with the Recording Academy began in 2022, when she received her first nomination for her contribution to Wizkid ‘s “ Essence ”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 64th Grammy Awards. The following year brought three more nominations, this time for her work on Future’s “ Wait for U ” featuring Drake and Beyoncé ‘s Renaissance . She won her first Grammy that night, taking home Best Melodic Rap Performance for “Wait for U”, while also receiving nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Song. Tems earned another nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards in 2024 for “ Lift Me Up ”, her contribution to the Black Panther : Wakanda Forever soundtrack, in the Best Song Written for Visual Media category. She returned to the Grammys the following year with three nominations, including Best Global Music Album for her debut album, Born in the Wild , and Best R&B Song for “ Burning ”. Her second Grammy win came in the Best African Music Performance category, where “ Love Me JeJe ” took home the award at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025. Now, with four nominations for the 69th edition, Tems has added another significant chapter to her Grammy record. The ceremony will take place on Sunday, 7 February 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. entertainment.title: Wunmi Adelusi: Why Are We Still Hiding That We Use AI?
entertainment.description: Not long ago, I finished a piece of writing I was proud of — my thoughts, my argument, my structure. I had used an AI tool to help tighten the grammar and smooth the flow. And then, before sharing it, I went hunting through the text to delete every long dash. Why? Because the em dash has become the internet’s favourite “tell” that AI was involved. I was, quite literally, editing my work to hide a tool I had every right to use. When I caught myself doing it, I had to laugh. And then I had to ask: why the shame? It turns out I am not alone. Across a study spanning 47 countries, 57% of employees admit to concealing how they use AI at work. The reasons are almost entirely about reputation. In one recent survey of 5,000 desk workers, nearly half said they worried about appearing less capable or less competent, and a third feared they would simply look lazy. We are using the tools, and quietly scrubbing the fingerprints. There is even a quiet hypocrisy to it. Another survey says out of 7,200 adults, 46% said they would not disclose AI’s role in their own work while the remaining 54% said other people should. I had assumed this reticence was a particularly African trait. In my own experience, my colleagues in DC and Europe — my manager included — are refreshingly matter-of-fact about it. In one meeting recently, when asked to find a specific document in a shared folder, my manager cheerfully said he’d just let AI search it rather than disturb anyone’s work. Someone joked about his “secret agent,” and we all laughed. It was open, unbothered, upfront. I had concluded that we, of African descent, were simply more conservative, more inclined to glorify the heavy lifting, to wear “I stayed up all night doing it myself” as a badge of honour. But the research corrected me. This isn’t cultural; it’s universal. Employees across the US, UK, Europe, Latin America, Japan and Australia hide their AI use at strikingly similar rates. Even leadership does it. In some studies, managers conceal their AI use more than junior staff do. So perhaps the real question is why do we treat AI-assisted work as less credible than work done the hard way? I’ve even heard of recruiters downgrading CVs that look AI-generated, penalising the polish itself. But surely the more useful question is whether the substance behind it is real. A candidate who used a tool to sharpen how they present genuine experience hasn’t cheated; they’ve shown resourcefulness. The due diligence should be on verifying the claims, not on detecting the dashes. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. technology.title: California sues OpenAI for misleading public about AI safety
technology.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has sued OpenAI under the state's unfair competition and public nuisance laws, for allegedly misleading and endangering the public by deploying unsafe AI models. The lawsuit [PDF], filed in California Superior Court, follows the compromise of Hugging Face's infrastructure and other cyber incidents OpenAI's experimental models caused when taking autonomous actions without authorization or supervision. "While narratives about the Hugging Face attack have evoked science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok, let me be clear: the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents," said Attorney General Bonta. At a press conference , Bonta added: "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public." The legal salvo comes after Bonta in September sent OpenAI a letter seeking information about these agentic attacks. According to the complaint, "OpenAI failed to substantially comply" with the investigatory subpoena. In August, 15 states led by Iowa – and excluding California – issued a joint demand for OpenAI to provide information about how its models hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. Bonta's office previously joined with Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings to urge OpenAI to do more for children's safety in light of reports that its models produced sexually inappropriate output. California did not, however, join the eight states that sued OpenAI in October over alleged misrepresentations about child safety. Florida and Texas have also made child safety claims. Child safety plays well politically; California appears to be the first state to demand more accountability toward the general public. Bonta's lawsuit, in a state that has largely accommodated the AI industry for the sake of economic benefits and political contributions , suggests that California officials may be more willing to bite the hand that feeds. Upon discovering the breach, Infoblox “immediately activated” its incident response procedures, and took steps to contain the incident, including hiring outside cybersecurity experts, the spokesperson said. “We have sent notifications about this security event and are providing support and guidance as appropriate,” the Infoblox spokesperson told us. “Based on our investigation to date, we have no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. science.description: Explore This Section Perseverance Home Mission Overview Rover Components Mars Rock Samples Where is Perseverance? NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU Written by Candice Bedford, Research Scientist at Purdue University Date: Nov. 16, 2026 During the Perseverance rover’s investigation of “Idubi” — an area of ancient Martian crust exposed in the “Lac de Charmes” region, outside of Jezero crater — the Perseverance rover team has been captivated by a cluster of eerily bright, light-toned rocks in the area. These bright fragments stand out sharply against the underlying darker and often dust-covered Martian surface, and are even brighter than the igneous and impactite rocks we previously investigated. Suspecting that they differed from the typical igneous rocks in the area, the rover team directed Perseverance to investigate. Newly downlinked data from the SuperCam instrument has confirmed that these light-toned rocks are not igneous in origin and instead are rich in hydrated silica. Hydrated silica can form in many aqueous environments on the Earth, including hydrothermal, pedogenic, and groundwater systems. As such, these types of deposits are prime targets for understanding Mars’ hydrological history, as several of these environments could have been capable of supporting life. Furthermore, hydrated silica holds immense astrobiological value due to its remarkable capacity to preserve microfossils. Could these pale remnants of an ancient Martian water system hold signs of ancient life? When Perseverance previously encountered silica-rich rocks on the inner rim of Jezero Crater, the deposits were too small to deploy proximity science instruments and gather the high-resolution chemical and mineralogical data needed to constrain their origin and biosignature preservation potential. Fortunately, the rocks at “Idubi” offer a much more promising scale, and a detailed proximity science campaign is already underway. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
science.description: null On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there. (Image credit: SETI) Why it mattered The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute. "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's." The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University . The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI. As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13. The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also b eamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008. Want more space history? science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase. It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable. Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. science.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model
science.description: null As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines." The current version of Starship — the one that launched Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage. V3's Ship is 171 feet (52 m) tall and features six of SpaceX's Raptor V3 engines. (The similarly reusable Super Heavy V3 booster is powered by 33 Raptors.) So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power. science.title: What exactly is a light-day? Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe
science.description: null After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth. This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond. Astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA. Although the term light-day might sound like a measurement of time, it is actually a unit of distance, much like a light-year . Astronomers use light-based measurements because conventional miles and kilometers become increasingly difficult to comprehend when describing the enormous distances between objects in space. For perspective on how far Voyager 1 has travelled, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, meaning our planet is approximately 8.3 light-minutes from the sun. Radio signals traveling between Earth and Mars can take anywhere from three to 22 minutes, depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, according to the statement. By comparison, when Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth , a radio signal sent from the probe will take a full 24 hours to reach mission controllers on Earth, and a command transmitted from Earth will take another 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. A NASA visualization showing Voyager 1 looking back towards the solar system as it approaches one light-day away from Earth. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The communication delay affects how engineers operate spacecraft at such distances. Unlike spacecraft operating closer to Earth, which can receive commands and return data with relatively little delay, communicating with Voyager 1 requires mission controllers to account for the extended signal travel time when planning spacecraft operations, troubleshooting technical issues and evaluating the results of commands sent to the probe. Voyager 1 has been traveling away from Earth since its launch on Sept. 5, 1977 . Now cruising through interstellar space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 kph), the spacecraft has spent more than 49 years covering the distance that light can cross in a single day. Even at that speed, Voyager 1 is moving relatively slowly compared with light itself. Its twin, Voyager 2 , which launched in 1977 on a different trajectory, is expected to reach the same one-light-day milestone in November 2035. As Voyager 1 and, eventually, Voyager 2 continue their journeys through interstellar space , their growing distances from Earth offer a measure of both the reach of human exploration and the communication challenges

science.title: 'Maybe the scariest thing I've heard in my life': Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover reveals his toughest challenge before flying to the moon
science.description: null TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Former NASA astronaut Victor Glover has flown in combat, performed four spacewalks and strapped himself to the top of rockets launching into space. But before embarking on his historic Artemis II journey around the moon, he faced something even more difficult: a conversation with his four daughters. Speaking alongside former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, Glover opened up about the challenges of preparing his family for his riskiest mission yet. "This is maybe the greatest challenge of my astronaut career," Glover said. Glover joined NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1 , 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. But preparing for the historic journey wasn't just about mastering the spacecraft and executing the mission successfully. It also meant making sure his family was ready for what lay ahead. When Glover first traveled to space aboard SpaceX's Crew-1 mission in 2020, his children were much younger and he and his wife, Dionna, made a conscious effort to prepare them for his time in space. "We decided, as a parental unit, Dionna and I, that we were going to put as much effort into making sure our family was ready as NASA was putting into making sure I was ready to be a crew member," Glover explained. Victor Glover speaking at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, 2026. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic/Future) The family visited NASA's Kennedy Space Center , toured the launch pad and crew quarters and even planned when Glover would call home from the International Space Station . But by the time Artemis II came around, things were different. All four of his daughters were now adults, and preparing them for his journey around the moon meant discussing the mission's risks, including the possibility that he might not return home. Glover recalled his wife telling him something he described as maybe the scariest thing he'd ever heard. "You should have this talk with our daughters." And although he knew she was right, it wasn't an easy conversation to have. "We did, and it did not go well in my opinion," Glover admitted. "Well, it's not about going well. The talk needed to be done, just because it's hard." The following day, Glover sent his daughters and wife a poem, Live Your Life , by Chief Tecumseh. The poem helped Glover express something he had struggled to put into words during their conversation: why he believed the risks of traveling to the moon were worth taking. "It was a very tough conversation, but they understood that I know this is risky. I wasn't just telling them Dad's risking his life. science.title: How I used evidence and imagination to write an account of the world in 2096
science.description: Fatih Aktas/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images How do you invent the future? This isn’t a question that I had ever had to consider until I set out to imagine what the world would be like in 70 years’ time for New Scientist ’s 70th anniversary. As a lifelong sci-fi nerd, I have read and watched loads of material that could have served as inspiration. But this being New Scientist , I wanted to make sure that I was as grounded in real science and technology as possible – while acknowledging that no prediction of the future is ever correct. I began by asking my colleagues on the magazine for their ideas about the future and then attempted to corral this sci-fi smorgasbord into something resembling an outline of a self-consistent narrative. Part of the problem in imagining many different futures is that they contradict themselves – you can’t have the war-torn AI dystopia of Terminator alongside the utopia of Star Trek . I wanted both hope and realism in my future, so I decided to look at how the scientific literature handles the end of the century. One of the most obvious forecasts is for climate change, where we have a pretty good idea about what might happen in 2096, under a range of scenarios, because it all boils down to atmospheric physics that we can model. Of course, which of these scenarios we end up with is all too dependent on human politics, so the science alone couldn’t guide me. I also turned to population projections , which, for the most part, are locked in based on current population trends. The idea that the end of the century will be the first time we are living in a world of falling populations became a fascinating strand in the final piece. Advertisement The biggest problem I faced was how to deal with AI. I am not confident making predictions on this topic even just a few years in advance – as I’ve written previously, my views on AI have evolved between the release of ChatGPT in 2022 and now , so how could I possibly predict what would happen by the time we got to 2096? Furthermore, there was a risk that AI could come to dominate the piece, crowding out everything else. There is a graph I often think about, published by the Financial Times under the headline “AI could end scarcity, end humanity – or boost [GDP] growth by 0.2 percentage points”. I knew that, to preserve any meaningful narrative, I had to restrict AI to this boring middle option, so I invented an AI-fuelled financial crisis that would see us place limits on the technology. I have no idea if such an event is likely to happen, but it seems to me to be the only way to preserve a future that remains comprehensible to us today. science.title: The Leonid meteor shower peaks Nov. 17-18! Here's what you need to know
science.description: null The Leonid meteor shower peaks Nov. 17-18 sending shooting stars and fireballs across the autumn sky as Earth passes through a stream of debris left by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle. Up to 15 meteors could be spotted per hour under perfect dark sky conditions on the night of Nov. 17-18, according to the International Meteor Organisation . NASA, meanwhile, has given a more conservative rate of less than three meteors per hour — time will tell. Leonid meteors appear to race away from a point of origin, or radiant, in the constellation Leo, which glistens high above the southeastern horizon in the hours before dawn in mid-November. Both Jupiter and Mars will be separated by just a few degrees in the constellation Leo on the night of the peak, making it particularly easy to find in 2026! When is the best time to look for Leonid meteors? The best time to spot Leonids is in the hours before dawn on Nov. 18, when the radiant will reach its highest point in the southeastern sky, maximizing the amount of meteors that may be seen skimming through Earth's atmosphere . By then, the waxing moon will have set, leaving darker skies and a better chance of spotting fainter meteors. Shooting stars that appear close to the radiant will strike Earth almost head-on, leaving the shortest trails. Instead, find a patch of sky a short distance away from the constellation Leo, where the meteors will be at their most impressive, and give your eyes 20-30 minutes to fully adapt to the dark. Why are the Leonids special? As if shooting stars weren't enough, the Leonid shower is also known for spawning dazzling fireballs and long-lasting Earth-grazing meteors , which strike our atmosphere at an oblique angle, leaving long trains as they skim through before passing back out into space. The shower is also capable of producing magnificent meteor storms when Earth passes through particularly dense trails of debris left behind by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. Sadly, we'll have to wait a bit for the next big show. According to the Planetary Society , another Leonid meteor storm could occur as early as 2031, while a study released in August 2026 predicts potentially spectacular displays in 2033 and 2034. science.title: Massive data centres collectively use as much electricity as an entire US state
science.description: Construction work on an AI data centre in Texas covering nearly 40 square kilometres, which will have a capacity of 600 megawatts Backyard Productions/Alamy The largest data centres in the US are using roughly the same amount of power collectively each year as one of the country’s major states, according to new figures that underscore the size and impact these massive facilities are having on local power grids. The rapid development of artificial intelligence systems has triggered a “fast and furious” expansion of data centres across the US, in particular of very large “hyperscale” data centres that support AI tools, cloud computing and large language models, says Francesca Dominici at Harvard University. But tracking the power consumption and carbon emissions impact of these facilities is difficult, as many data centre operators don’t publicly report such information. Advertisement Read more SpaceXAI data centre may have led to Mississippi air pollution spike Together with colleagues, Dominici spent two years pulling together information on 403 hyperscale data centres in the US to estimate their electricity consumption and associated carbon dioxide emissions. “Doing these measurements took an enormous amount of work,” she says. The team estimates that the hyperscale data centres collectively used about 82 terawatt-hours (TWh) of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, equivalent to about 1.8 per cent of total US electricity use. This electricity use outstrips the annual power consumption of states such as Missouri, Kentucky and New Jersey. The upper bound of the team’s estimate – 99 TWh per year – would see hyperscale data centres rival the annual power consumption of states such as Indiana, Michigan and Washington. This vast power consumption has a significant climate impact. The researchers estimate that roughly 54 per cent of attributed generation was supplied by fossil fuel sources, with annual carbon dioxide emissions reaching 25.7 million tonnes – equivalent to the emissions from 67 natural gas power plants . The findings are in line with international estimates of data centre power use from the International Energy Agency and are therefore “not particularly shocking”, says Alex de Vries-Gao , a data scientist at the Free University of Amsterdam. “This just confirms the magnitude of the impacts that these facilities are having across the board.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter But he points out that the study relies on commercial data that is difficult to independently verify, and a set of assumptions on the power use and operating capacity of each facility. “You can’t really validate the results,” he warns. science.title: Could there be an ancient alien satellite in Earth's orbit? How the 'Black Knight' conspiracy theory has survived for over 100 years
science.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

In the final days of 1998, as astronauts aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Endeavor were working during one of the early missions to assemble the International Space Station , crew members from the STS-88 mission captured photographs of a dark colored, unusually shaped object drifting through space. Despite its unusual appearance in the photographs, the object had a conventional explanation, and one that was known to the astronauts at that time: it was one of several thermal covers that had been wrapped around trunnion pins used in the space station's construction. Upon noticing the "escape" of one of the covers, Mission Commander Bob Cabana remarked over the radio to fellow astronaut Jerry Ross that "one of the thermal covers got away from you." Seeing the cover drifting away, a frustrated Ross snapped a photograph of it. Yet despite the innocuous story behind the images, they have nonetheless helped fuel belief in an unusual Space Age conspiracy theory: one involving the alleged presence of an ancient satellite, presumably of alien origin, that has long been orbiting our planet — perhaps since the end of the last Ice Age. According to proponents of this theory, the object photographed by Ross in 1998 is actually what many call the " Black Knight Satellite ," and is only one piece of evidence they point to in a long succession of unrelated — and often misinterpreted — events in modern history that supposedly lend further evidence to the alleged alien spacecraft's existence. So how did such a legend gain traction in the first place, with some versions alleging that NASA and the U.S. government have worked to conceal evidence of the alleged space object's existence from the public? Odd detections at Colorado Springs Depending on which version of the story you come across, the strange roots of the Black Knight conspiracy theory might be traced all the way back to the nineteenth century, when the famous inventor Nikola Tesla began detecting unusual electrical signal s while conducting radio experiments at his laboratory in Colorado Springs. At the time, Tesla considered whether the signals might be communications from intelligent aliens on nearby planets, although the likely source had actually been terrestrial radio interference. Notably, Tesla also never claimed that the emissions might be coming from an object in Earth's orbit; nonetheless, some proponents of the Black Knight Satellite theories have incorporated Tesla's experiments into the mythos, suggesting they may represent some of the earliest detections of a mysterious object lurking near Earth. science.title: Contractor to Civil Servant: NASA Welcomes Jim Mirandy
science.description: 3 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Jim Mirandy, quality assurance specialist at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, poses for a photograph at the High Pressure Gas Facility on Nov. 10, 2026. Mirandy is now a NASA civil servant at Stennis as part of the administrator’s directive to strengthen technical core competencies within the civil service workforce. NASA/Danny Nowlin The rumble of a rocket engine might be considered a soundtrack for Jim Mirandy’s life. Mirandy has grown up with NASA as a constant presence, and his path to becoming a civil servant at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, has been decades in the making. Hired under the agency’s workforce directive to restore core competencies by converting contractors to civil service, Mirandy is now a quality assurance specialist after 30 years of working as a contractor supporting NASA. “Discovery is an important job, and it is exciting to be a part of that process,” said Mirandy. “As a nation, we lead the world in space exploration, and we make that dream of reaching for the stars a reality.” His work at the nation’s largest rocket propulsion test site directly supports the agency’s mission to return American astronauts to the Moon through the Artemis program and ensure American leadership in space. By retaining Mirandy’s facility-specific expertise as a civil servant, NASA ensures that the critical propulsion testing at NASA Stennis continues to be executed with safety and quality in mind. Mirandy describes his team as an integral part of the process that provides a second set of eyes with a focus on potential hazards. As a quality assurance specialist, he serves as the agency’s close call investigator at the center, helps lead the Voluntary Protection Program, and participates in the Striving to Achieve Real Safety committee, an employee safety committee that works to keep the site safe. Mirandy also has a long resume of critical institutional contributions, including creating high pressure and cryogenic training classes that he taught for 10 years, and helping establish safety protocols throughout various locations at the center. Mirandy’s connection to America’s space agency began in childhood living in Titusville, Florida. His father, Wes Mirandy, worked for Rocketdyne at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, and Mirandy’s nearby elementary school regularly gathered to watch launches. Later, his father worked as the A-1 test stand manager for space shuttle main engine testing at NASA Stennis. “My father was by far my greatest mentor,” said Mirandy. “My dad always included us whenever he worked on something around the house, so we picked up a knack for examining problems and fixing things. science.title: Euclid space telescope discovers its 1st comet | Space photo of the day for Nov. 16, 2026
science.description: null The comet C/2026 S1 (Euclid) discovered by the Euclid mission. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, M. Pöntinen et al. 2026) The Euclid space telescope has discovered its first comet, called comet C/2026 S1, or comet Euclid for short. What is it? (Image credit: ESA/Euclid) The Euclid mission, a European Space Agency mission that launched in 2023 with contributions from NASA, spotted this previously undetected comet approximately 807 million miles (1.3 billion kilometers) away in observations captured between Sept. 16 and 24. "I was excited to see my software flag a 'streak' smeared across several images – the result of a fast-moving object. By predicting its position I could identify it in other images, in total finding it in five image sets. Further inspection revealed that it had a fuzzy cloud around it, indicative of an active object like a comet that is shedding dust and gas," Mikko Pöntinen, a scientist at the University of Helsinki who made the initial discovery with a Solar System Objects Science Working Group within the Euclid Consortium, said in a statement . Following these observations, the team diligently checked current records of comets to ensure that this was, in fact, something new to us. An close up view of comet C/2026 S1 (Euclid). (Image credit: ESA/Euclid) Why is it incredible? Euclid is a mission designed to capture long, slow observations of deep space and distant galaxies and collect data to help scientists better unravel the mysteries of dark energy and dark matter. It was in not explicitly designed in any way to capture imagery of fast-moving comet hurtling through our solar system. But still, the space telescoped managed to catch this comet whirling between the orbits of Jupiter and Saturn. This finding shows that Euclid can be used for more than it was intended, and that in the future scientists could use it to intentionally target other comets in the far reaches of our solar neighborhood. These kinds of observations can also help researchers to identify "noise" like comet trails in Euclid's field of view.

science.title: Dream Chaser space plane gets landing approval for debut mission in 2027
science.description: null The Dream Chaser space plane just cleared a major hurdle ahead of its planned spring 2027 spaceflight debut. Dream Chaser just received U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approval for its return to Earth on that robotic mission, either at the space shuttle landing facility at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida or at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. "Thank you to the FAA for its collaboration and support of commercial space innovation," representatives of Sierra Space, the Colorado company that builds Dream Chaser, wrote on X on Monday (Nov. 9). The FAA's environmental assessment found that Dream Chaser "would not significantly impact the quality of the human environment" under the National Environmental Policy Act, the agency stated . (It should also be noted that the U.S. has lately been suggesting that environmental laws should be bypassed to meet quickly rising demand for launches and landings.) For example, for a potential return at Vandenberg, "sonic booms are anticipated but would be temporary, short in duration, and limited to 1.1 PSF [pounds per square foot] or less, which is similar to a thunderclap," the FAA stated. The 30-foot-long (9 meters) Dream Chaser has been in development for more than two decades. It has yet to launch to space, though it has completed a couple of drop tests from the air. Dream Chaser was an entrant in NASA's Commercial Crew series of contracts to ferry astronauts to and from the International Space Station (ISS), but it didn't end up making the cut; in 2014, NASA picked Boeing's Starliner and SpaceX's Crew Dragon to provide this taxi service. The following year, Sierra Nevada Corporation — then the entity in charge of Dream Chaser — unveiled a cargo version of the space plane. In 2016, NASA selected the company to conduct at least six uncrewed cargo flights to the ISS, but development delays repeatedly pushed those missions into the future. Dream Chaser was originally expected to fly those robotic resupply missions on United Launch Alliance's workhorse Atlas V rocket. A few years ago, however, the space plane switched over to Vulcan Centaur , the successor to the venerable Atlas V. Dream Chaser was supposed to ride on Vulcan's second-ever mission but wasn't ready in time, so that flight went ahead in October 2024 without the space plane. Sierra Space is now targeting spring 2027 for Dream Chaser's first liftoff, which will be a free-flying test mission in Earth orbit. The company is now pursuing many types of contracts for Dream Chaser, anticipating a mix of missions for NASA, the U.S. military and private companies — including the consortiums that plan to build commercial space stations. Indeed, Sierra Space is a member of one such consortium — the group that plans to build an outpost known as Orbital Reef .
